title: Casper and the Kitchen
premise: Freya Almeida has spent five years quietly rebuilding her life in her late grandfather's lighthouse cottage, writing novels by day and answering letters from a mysterious correspondent named Casper by night. When a man named Casper Reyes moves into the neighboring cottage, Freya assumes coincidence — until she discovers he is the letter-writer, and that he has been dying of a degenerative illness he never mentioned, writing to her as a way to leave something behind. As their friendship deepens into love, Freya must confront the memory of the accident that made her retreat from the world, while Casper must forgive himself for a past failure that haunts his reflection. In the end, Casper's surgery offers uncertain hope rather than certainty, and Freya chooses to love him without guarantees, opening her home, her heart, and her unfinished novel to a future they build together one small brave step at a time.
about_author: Dominic Nystrom is a former lighthouse tender's assistant who turned to fiction after a decade spent cataloguing maritime letters for a coastal historical society. He writes quiet romances about people who repair themselves the way they repair old things: slowly, honestly, and with salt-stained hands.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Hours
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. We meet Freya maintaining the decommissioned lighthouse, teaching a weekly writing class, and drafting her nightly reply to 'Casper,' her decade-long pen pal whose letters she has never answered with her real address. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness; she guards her routines like the light itself.

chapters.title: A Moving Truck in November
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A quiet man named Casper Reyes moves into the crumbling cottage next door, and Freya is rattled by the shared name and his uncanny familiarity with her habits. She tests him with details only her correspondent would know; he deflects. Emotional beat: suspicion tangled with an unwanted spark of hope.

chapters.title: Salt and Static
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper recognizes Freya instantly — he chose the cottage deliberately — but hides both his identity and his diagnosis, terrified of being pitied. He helps her repair storm-damaged shutters, and their easy rhythm unsettles him. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into self-loathing as he watches her trust him.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Keeps
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A tremor in his hand forces Casper to confront his worsening symptoms and the memory of the brother he failed to save, the reason he believes he doesn't deserve care. He writes Freya a letter he cannot send. Emotional beat: grief surfacing; forgiveness begins to seem possible but not yet earned.

chapters.title: The Unsent Drawer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya finds Casper's discarded drafts blown against her fence, including one addressed in the handwriting from her letters. Confronted, he admits everything except his illness. Feeling manipulated, she shuts him out. Emotional beat: betrayal and heartbreak; the found family she was building cracks.

chapters.title: Winter Without Letters
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks of silence; Freya throws herself into finishing her novel, while Casper's health declines alone. His estranged sister arrives, forcing him to reckon with the family he pushed away. Emotional beat: both realize the other had become home; pride proves heavier than fear.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Question
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper collapses during a storm and Freya finds him, learning the truth of his illness from his sister. Furious and frightened, she nevertheless keeps vigil through the night, reading his unsent letters aloud. Emotional beat: anger transmuting into tenderness; she chooses presence over protection.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya finally tells Casper about the accident that killed her grandfather and taught her to live cautiously, and he tells her why he believes he forfeited the right to be loved. They forgive each other first, themselves second. Emotional beat: mutual confession; intimacy built on truth instead of letters.

chapters.title: Running Out of Light
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper qualifies for a risky surgery scheduled in six weeks, and his deterioration accelerates. He asks Freya not to wait for him; she answers by moving his desk beside hers and reading him the ending of her novel, which he inspired. Emotional beat: terror met with defiance; love declared without conditions.

chapters.title: Casper and the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Surgery day. The operation is long and its outcome uncertain, but Casper survives with partial recovery — no promises, only time. Months later they share the kitchen of the keeper's cottage, his sister at the table, Freya's finished novel on the counter. Emotional beat: resolution; found family assembled, identities forgiven, futures unwritten together.
